summary: VerdantCare private deployment — 3 hour gap in audit log ingestion causing regulatory escalation
description: Issue summary: VerdantCare reported missing audit log events for a 3-hour window (2026-03-10 06:12–09:15 UTC) from their private deployment. Missing entries contain authentication and PII access events required for HIPAA audits. Impact: Compliance exposure for VerdantCare; customer escalated to legal and compliance teams and requested immediate evidence and remediation.
timeline:
2026-03-10 06:10 UTC: VerdantCare alert via webhook: "Audit ingestion lag > 120s"
2026-03-10 06:25 UTC: Support triage assigned (SUP-847654 created).
2026-03-10 06:40 UTC: SRE observed audit-processor consumer lag and backpressure to control plane.
2026-03-10 07:05 UTC: Control plane metrics show increased retry rate to S3 archive (~5x).
2026-03-10 07:40 UTC: Root cause identified as KMS key rotation that caused transient access-denied errors to S3 archive for encrypted blobs.
2026-03-10 08:10 UTC: Hotfix deployed to skip backfilled writes to primary S3 path and persist to temporary partition (local encrypted bucket).
2026-03-10 09:15 UTC: Catch-up job completed; ingestion gap closed.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC: VerdantCare provided confirmation of restored entries and accepted temporary evidence package.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Private control plane with customer-managed KMS rotated key at 06:02 UTC.
2) Audit-processor attempts to re-encrypt and upload queued audit blobs to customer's S3 path.
3) KMS returns AccessDenied for ~100% of re-encrypt attempts until key alias reconciled.
4) Backpressure triggers consumer pause and buffer-growth; control plane retries amplify the queue.
sample_logs:
[2026-03-10T06:07:12Z] audit-processor ERROR upload_blob s3://verdantcare-audit/2026/03/10/06/ audit_id=abc123 err=AccessDenied: KMS key not found
[2026-03-10T06:07:13Z] control-plane WARN consumer_lag=1240 buffer_size=3821
[2026-03-10T07:02:01Z] kms-manager INFO detected_key_rotation alias=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/xxxx
[2026-03-10T07:05:03Z] audit-processor INFO retry upload_blob attempt=12 audit_id=abc123 status=throttled
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: KMS rotation in customer's account momentarily invalidated permissions used by the private control plane to write encrypted blobs to the S3 archive. Evidence: S3 PutObjectAccessDenied errors correlated exactly with KMS rotation window; cloudtrail events show Decrypt denied for control-plane role. Reproduced in staging by forcing KMS alias swap and observing identical consumer lag and AccessDenied symptoms. Metrics: audit-processor consumer lag peaked at 3,900 entries; retry storms caused >2x CPU on audit-processor pods leading to delayed backoff and ripple into other pipelines. Alternate hypotheses (network flaps, S3 throttling) ruled out by steady S3 200 rates outside rotation window and absence of network errors on instances.

resolution: Root cause: Customer-side KMS alias rotation caused temporary AccessDenied on re-encrypt/upload path for audit blobs. Fixes applied: 1) Hotfix to audit-processor to resolve alias-to-key lookup and to gracefully fall back to local encrypted partition when uploads fail due to KMS errors. 2) Catch-up job to reprocess buffered blobs and backfill S3 archive with preserved timestamps. 3) Added an end-to-end test in CI that simulates KMS alias swap and verifies audit ingestion resiliency. Customer accepted evidence package; no PII loss confirmed.
